May last year I said I would take a break. Then, at the end of last year, I tried to start up again. But it wasn’t that easy. I still have all kinds of things I want to write about. I also don’t want to abandon the Agile angle of my publication. But I haven’t found a new niche, something I can deeply invest in as I did before. That said, I’m still working as an organisational coach, and I come across many things that strike me. Today I am sharing an experience piece about how AI can’t solve all your problems. We still need the human factor. Here are four examples of how AI usage (alone) can miss the mark. This article is 100% human. No AI was used to create it. Faster delivery The first example is about a company showing pride in their achievement of improving development teams’ delivery times from 7 days on average to 5 days by using AI. That’s a gain of almost 30%! This is quite impressive. However, there were a few caveats. It still took 1.5 months on average for a request to land on the desk of the development team. Nothing was gained there. Also, it still took 2 months on average for a client to enjoy the newly developed solutions. Clients had to wait a long time, even after bringing the product live. -- -- Written by Willem-Jan Ageling 20K followers · 199 following https://ageling.substack.com Writer, editor, founder of Serious Scrum.
